content: Have you ever seen a little bird shivering in the rain? Where does it go when it storms? Where do you go when it rains heavily outside?
Imagine if we lived outside in the open all the time. What would happen if it rained, or if it was very hot, or if a wild animal came by? Why do you think we build walls around us?

content.title: Finding Shelter
content.description: A house protects us from the weather outside.

content: A house is a place where we live. It protects us from heat, cold, rain, wind, and wild animals.

definition: A building where people live, providing shelter and safety.

question: Why do we need a house?
options: To protect us from rain and heat

content: Think about your own house. What is your favorite thing about it? Does it feel safe when you are inside?
Just like humans build houses, animals also build homes! A bird builds a nest, a bee builds a hive.
Draw a picture of your house and color it. Show it to your parents and tell them why you feel safe inside.
Have you seen houses in villages with roofs made of dry grass? And tall buildings in the city made of strong concrete? Why do they look so different?
If you want to build a house that will never fall down even in a strong storm, what materials would you use? Straw and mud, or bricks and cement?

content.title: Kutcha and Pucca Houses
content.description: Different houses are made of different materials.

content: There are two main types of houses. Kutcha houses are made of mud, straw, and wood. Pucca houses are made of bricks, cement, iron, and glass.

definition: A temporary house made of natural materials like mud, straw, and bamboo.
A strong, permanent house made of bricks, cement, steel, and stones.

question: Which material is used to build a Pucca house?

content: Look at the walls of the room you are in right now. What do you think they are made of? Are you in a Kutcha or a Pucca house?
Long ago, early humans didn't know how to build houses! They lived in caves to stay safe.
Mini challenge: Gather some building blocks or Lego pieces and try to build the strongest Pucca house you can!
Remind students of the story of the Three Little Pigs to help them remember the difference between strong and weak materials.
Students sometimes think only tall buildings are Pucca houses. Clarify that even a small one-story home can be a Pucca house if made of bricks and cement.
Have you ever tried sleeping in the kitchen? Or taking a bath in the living room? That sounds very silly, right?
Why do we divide a house into different rooms? Imagine if a house was just one giant room where everyone cooked, slept, and bathed together!
A house has different rooms for different activities. We cook in the kitchen, sleep in the bedroom, bathe in the bathroom, and welcome guests in the living room.

question: In which room do we cook our food?

content: Which room in your house do you spend the most time in? Why is it your favorite?
In some very small houses, one single room is used for sleeping, eating, and sitting! This teaches us to be grateful for the space we have.
Play a guessing game with a friend. Act out an activity (like sleeping or brushing teeth) and ask them to guess which room you are in!
Kids often confuse 'living room' with 'bedroom' because they 'live' in their bedrooms. Clarify that living room is for the whole family and guests.
